bynnac: bynnac (bynnag) — -ever, indefinite particle after peth/pwy etc.; 'Peth bynnac' 'whatever'
y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that')
buant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (Ny buant 'they were not')
ar: ar — (1) preposition 'on, upon; at' (ar Hafgan; ar y carw; ar y gilyd 'against the other'); (2) the article yr after a vowel, 'that which' (noc ar a uu 'than what was'; Ar ny del 'and whoever does not come') · also (3) 'with, accompanied by' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen'); 'in' (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses'; ar perued y digrifwch 'in the middle of the merriment'); ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'; ar uyrr 'quickly'; ar hynny 'thereupon' (see yny) · also 'over' (ar yr ynys hon 'over this island'); 'after the manner of' (ar ureint kyweirdeb 'in the manner of the arrangement'); 'on' a decision (disgynnu ar gymryt hynny 'settled on taking that'); 'ar ol' 'after' (ar ol Matholwch 'after Matholwch'); ar dec 'on ten' (see dec) · also 'concerning, about', where am would be expected (ac ar Yspydaut Benn 'and concerning the Hospitality of the Head'; the Red Book also ar)
wynt: wynt (hwynt) — they, them; 3 pl. pronoun (un lliw ac wynt 'the same colour as them') · also Wynt, Gwent, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed', a region of south-east Wales
a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six') · also 'to, towards' with spirant mutation (parth a Hardlech 'towards Harlech'; y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall')
doethant: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Y'r llys y doethant 'to the court they came')
dyuet: Dyuet (Dyfed) — proper name, the region of south-west Wales
ac: a — 'and' before a vowel (ac ef); also the preposition a 'with' before a vowel (ymgael ac ef 'meet with him', ymordiwes ac ef) · the manuscript also writes ac before some consonants (Ac wal, Ac val, ac racdaw) · also 'as' after an equative or kymeint (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'; mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'as unseemly as what she had done')
arberth: Arberth (Arberth) — proper name, Pwyll's chief court, modern Narberth in Dyfed
gyrchyssant: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they made for', soft-mutated after a (Yr orssed a gyrchyssant 'they made for the mound')
llad: llad (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun, base form (y'm llad i 'to kill me') · also llad glwm 'to tie a knot' (idiomatic, literally 'strike a knot'): llad glwm ar garryeu y got 'to tie a knot on the straps of the bag'
tan: tan (tân) — fire; noun m. (y tan a'r glo 'the fire and the charcoal'); no mutation
wnaethant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (eisted a wnaethant)
dechreu: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor 'beginning to muster') · also the noun 'beginning' (ar dechreu kyuedach 'at the start of the carousing')
ymborth: ymborth (ymborth) — (1) food, sustenance (y caffom yn ymborth 'that we may get as sustenance'); (2) as verbal noun, to feed, live (on) (dechreu a wnaethant ymborth ar kic hela 'they began to live on the meat of the chase'); noun m. / verbal noun; radical
hela: hela (hela) — to hunt; verbal noun (uynet y hela 'to go to hunt')
threulaw: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A threulaw a wnaethant)
mis: mis (mis) — month; noun m. (pethewnos a mis 'a fortnight and a month'; y pedwyryd mis 'the fourth month'); no mutation
yuelly: yuelly (felly) — thus, so, in that way; adverb, the particle y fused with uelly (a chyt kerych di uot yuelly 'though you wish it to be so'; Ac yuelly y gwnaethpwyt 'and so it was done'); no mutation
cwn: ci (ci) — dogs; noun pl. of ci, the pack as individual animals (as against erchwys, the pack as a body)
attunt: at (at) + wynt — 'to them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (a doeth attunt 'came to them'); no mutation
bot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun (hyt na bo... uot 'so that there be...') · also introducing a reported fact, 'that (it) was' (adnabot bot eu hennill yn pallu 'knowing that their gain was failing'; clybot bot y gwyr 'hearing that the men were')
yno: yno (yno) — there; adverb (ac yno y bu y nos honno)
ulwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f., soft-mutated after y/the feminine article (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn) · also adverbial, 'a year' in time phrases, soft-mutated without the article (ulwydyn y heno 'a year from tonight'; ual yd eistedyssant ulwydyn o'r nos honno 'as they sat a year from that night'), the soft mutation being that of an adverbial accusative of time · also soft after a preceding ordinal (y seithuet ulwydyn 'the seventh year')
kyuodi: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; verbal noun (kyuodi a oruc 'he rose')
pryderi: Pryderi (Pryderi) — proper name, the son of Pwyll and Rhiannon, named from pryder 'care'; no mutation
manawydan: Proper name — Manawydan, son of Llŷr, brother of Bendigeidfran; radical (subject, after a 'and')
chyweiraw: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to arrange, put in order, prepare; verbal noun (A chyweiraw y pebylleu 'and arranging the tents'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
mynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun (amser mynet y uwyta 'time to go to eat')
odieithyr: odieithyr (oddieithr) — outside of; except; preposition (odieithyr y porth 'outside the gate'); no mutation
llys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., base form
sef: sef (sef) — it is (this), that is; presentative particle introducing an explanation or answer
wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a; auxiliary in 'verbal noun + a wnaeth' (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth)
rei: rei (rhai) — some, some people; pronoun (rei o'r maes hwnn 'some of this field')
o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
e: y — 'his', spelt e before a following consonant or in some spellings: e gwn 'his dogs', e weneb 'his face'; also the preposition 'to' in e uynet 'to go' · also 'her', with h- before a vowel (e hymlit hi 'to pursue her'); the verbal particle y (e deuthum i 'I came'); y of y wrth 'from' (e wrthaw 'from him'); and in e uynyd 'up', e ymdeith 'away' · also the article 'the' (E brenhin, E chwedyl 'the king', 'the news'); 'it' as dummy subject (E doeth im 'it came to me') · also the infixed object 'him' after a (pwy a'e lladei 'who killed him'; a'e guelei 'who saw him') and 'her' with spirant mutation (a'e chladu yno 'and burying her there'); and the y of y gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also in e hun (ehun) 'self, own', unchanged for any person (eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions'; synnyaw e hun 'watching for himself')
kerdet: kerdet (cerdded) — going, walking; verbal noun, also a noun 'pace, gait' (kerdet araf guastat 'a slow, even pace'; o'r kerdet mwyaf 'to the greatest pace')
uechan: bychan (bychan, bach) — small; feminine bechan, soft-mutated (b > u) after a feminine noun (got uechan 'a small bag')
oed: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect 'was' (Pwyll... a oed yn arglwyd) · also oed 'appointed time, tryst', noun m., = oet (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
gyr: ger (ger) — near, beside; preposition, spelt gyr (gyr y bron 'beside her breast'; gyr llaw hwnnw 'beside that'); no mutation
llaw: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., in the idiom uch llaw 'above, overlooking' (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also gyr llaw 'beside, next to' (eisted gyr llaw hwnnw 'to sit beside it') · also 'hand' without mutation after the article y (yn y llaw arall 'in the other hand')
gyt: kyt (cyd) — together; in y gyt (a) 'together (with)' (y gyt ac wynt 'together with them')
yd: yd — preverbal particle used when the clause opens with an adverb rather than the subject, introducing an indicative main verb (A threigylgweith yd oed yn Arberth)
r: 'r — the article yr contracted after a vowel, apostrophe half of a'r, y'r, o'r etc.: 'the'
kilyaw: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat, withdraw, fall back; verbal noun (nyt oes gynghor namyn kilyaw 'there is no counsel but to retreat')
gyflym: kyflym (cyflym) — swift; adjective, soft-mutated (k>g) after yn (yn gyflym caeu y got 'quickly shutting the bag')
mawr: mawr (mawr) — big, great; adjective (uarch erchlas mawr 'a big dapple-grey horse')
ganthunt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with them' (ni bu newydach ganthunt 'it was no more novel to them')
ymchwelut: ymchwelut (ymchwelyd) — to turn (oneself); verbal noun (ymchwelut e weneb at yr erchwyn)
at: at — preposition 'to, towards' (at y cwn 'to the dogs')
guyr: gwr (gŵr) — man; plural guyr 'men' (gwŷr); gu- for gw-; no mutation (Y guyr hynny 'those men', after the article)
heb: heb — (1) 'said' (heb ef 'said he'), a defective verb used only for tagging speech; (2) 'without' + verbal noun (heb hanbwyllaw 'without troubling') · (3) 'past, beside' in heb law (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound'); see hebdaw · also 'without' + noun (heb ohir 'without delay')
parth: parth (parth) — towards, side, direction; noun m./preposition (parth a'y lys 'towards his court')
edrych: edrych (edrych) — to look; verbal noun (edrych ar y carw 'to look at the stag')
beth: beth — what; interrogative pronoun (beth amgen 'what else?', beth a wnaf 'what shall I do?')
yssyd: bot (bod) — to be; relative present 'is, who/that is' (sydd) (Gwr yssyd gyuerbyn; pa amgen uedwl yssyd yndaw)
yndi: yn (yn) + hi — conjugated preposition 'in her/it', feminine (Nit oes yndi nep; y guassanaeth yndi)
nessau: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; verbal noun (yn nessau yn ebrwyd attunt 'drawing near swiftly to them'); no mutation
pan: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction with a past-time clause (pan doeth) · also interrogative 'from where, whence' (pan doy di? 'where do you come from?')
llyma: llyma (dyma) — behold, here is; presentative particle throwing a scene before the reader (llyma yr erchwys)
yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was') · also yn yd 'as, while, when' (Ac yn yd aeth pawb ym pen yr arueu 'and while all went to arms'; the sense uncertain) · also 'our', a spelling of an (ein), with no mutation (yn anniuer ninheu 'our own company'; yn ymborth 'our sustenance'; yn diuetha 'our destroying')
oruc: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite auxiliary 'he did', soft-mutated after a, with g dropped (kyuodi a oruc)
idaw: idaw (iddo) — to him; 3 sg. m. conjugated form of y 'to'
ynteu: ynteu (yntau) — 'he, for his part'; conjunctive pronoun marking a change of speaker or actor (heb ynteu)
adaw: adaw (gadael) — to leave; verbal noun, a form without g- (A dyuot cof idaw adaw y drws yn agoret 'and he remembered leaving the door open'); no mutation
dalym: talym (talym) — a while, space of time; noun m. (dalym o'r nos 'a while of the night'); soft-mutated (t>d) as an adverbial object after the verb
wrth: wrth (wrth) — to, towards, according to; preposition, base form (dywedut... wrthaw) · also 'at' (wrth y danned 'at the teeth'; wrth yr ascwrn 'at the bone') and 'because of' (wrth hynny 'for that reason')
yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon', kept as written (the Red Book has ar hynny) (Ac ar yny, llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the warband')
uei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might be', soft-mutated after a (a uei uwy no hynny) · also soft-mutated after ban 'when' (ban uei uwyaf 'when it was most')
agos: agos (agos) — near, close; adjective/adverb (o agos 'from near'); no mutation (vowel)
rodei: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. imperfect 'she would give' (ni rodei hi 'she would not give'); mutation of rh- not visible in spelling
phan: pan (pan) — when; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A phan doeth yno) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no phan uuassei 'than when he had been')
ol: ol (ôl) — track, trace; noun m. (yn ol y cwn 'after the hounds'; yn y ol 'in its track')
welynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. imperfect 'they saw', soft-mutated after a (wynt a welynt 'they saw'; yny welynt 'until they saw')
uawr: mawr (mawr) — great, big; adjective (grauanc uawr 'a great claw'); soft-mutated (m>u) after a feminine noun · also predicative, soft-mutated directly after the verb (nyt oed uawr y weilgi 'the sea was not great')
aruchel: aruchel (aruchel) — very high, lofty; adjective, ar- + uchel 'high' (mawr aruchel 'big and very tall')
gueith: gweith (gwaith) — work, labour, craft, the thing made; noun m., gu- spells gw- (o'r gueith hwnnw 'of that work'; y gueith wynteu 'their work'); radical after the article and after y standing for eu 'their'
arnei: ar — conjugated preposition 'on her' (a charyat arnei 'and love on her') · also 'on it', of a feminine noun (a eistedo arnei 'who may sit on it', of the mound)
lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form
ny: ny (ni/nid) — negative particle 'not', base form before a consonant with soft mutation · also spirant mutation of c, p, t (ny chewch 'you will not get'; ny thygyawd 'it did not avail'); soft mutation of g (ny wybydei 'knew not')
welsynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had seen' in -synt (na welsynt eiryoet 'that they had never seen'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the negative na · also soft after the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'all they had seen of grief')
na: na — (1) negative particle in a subordinate clause, 'not' (na dywedy di); (2) 'neither/nor' in a series (na guas ystauell, na swydawc) · also negative imperative 'do not', with soft mutation (na ouyn di 'do not ask'; na yrrwch geu arnaf 'do not lay a lie on me'; na hawl ef 'do not claim him')
eiryoet: eiryoet (erioed) — ever; variant spelling of eiroet (o'r a welsei eiryoet 'of all he had ever seen')
kyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun (Kyrchu y llys a oruc ynteu)
yr: yr — (1) the article 'the' before a vowel (yr erchwys); (2) 'for, for the sake of' preposition (yr Duw 'for God's sake', yr guaret gormes 'for removing the oppression') · (3) 'for all, however' before an equative-type noun and a clause (yr araued y kerdei y uarch 'for all the slowness with which his horse went'); (4) in yr meityn 'for a while (since)'; (5) the verbal particle y, yd, written yr before a vowel (yr ymordiwedei a hi 'that he would overtake her') · also (6) the perfective particle ry written yr, softening the verb (yr gyscwys 'has slept'); the article before an independent possessive (yr eidunt 'theirs'); 'for' with an abstract noun (yr bychanet 'for the smallness') · also the article before hwnn, honn, 'the one' (yr hwnn y tu a Chernyw 'the one on the side towards Cornwall'; yr honn a uu tryded anuat paluawt 'the one that was the third unfortunate blow') · also yr (er) 'for all' before the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'for all the grief they had seen')
guedy: guedy (gwedi) — after; preposition (A guedy y medwl hwnnw 'and after that thought')
welet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, soft-mutated after dy 'your' (dy welet ti 'seeing you', literally 'your seeing') · also soft after o 'from, because of' (o welet gwr kymeint a gerynt 'from seeing a man so loved by them') · also soft after am 'for, because of' (am welet y cledyf 'for seeing the sword')
weith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, make, pattern, manner; noun m. (MW gweith); g lost by soft mutation after ar (ar weith taryaneu da 'after the pattern of good shields, on the work of good shields'); the sense 'manner, pattern' is a little uncertain
kyn: kyn (cyn) — before; with a verbal noun (kyn uy rodi 'before my being given') · also the equative particle 'as', softening the adjective (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy') · also 'although', with the subjunctive (Kyn ny bwyf arglwydes 'though I am not a lady')
no: no (na) — than, comparative particle (no gyrru 'than driving'; no chyuedach)
hynny: hynny — 'that (thing)'; demonstrative pronoun, very frequent (a hynny 'and that')
ben: pen (pen) — head; noun m. (ar y ben 'on his head'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the possessive y 'his'
orssed: gorssed (gorsedd) — mound; noun f., g lost by soft mutation after the article, as a feminine noun (yr orssed 'the mound', y'r orssed 'to the mound')
ymwarandaw: ymwarandaw (ymwrando) — to listen (to, with a); verbal noun (yn ymwarandaw a llef yr erchwys)
pa: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative adjective, triggers soft mutation of the following noun
hyt: hyt (hyd) — as far as, until; preposition/conjunction (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end'; hyt na bo 'so that there be not') · also ar hyt 'along' (ar hyt y prifford 'along the highway') · also 'as far as, so far as, as much as, to the extent that' with the subjunctive (hyt y mynnych 'as much as you wish'; hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it'); hyt oet y wled 'until the time of the feast' · also 'so that' with the indicative (hyt nat oed rym 'so that there was no use'); hyt yn Aberfraw 'as far as Aberffraw' · also the noun 'length, duration' after pa 'what' (Pa hyt bynnac y bydynt ar y ford 'however long they were on the road')
bydynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. habitual imperfect 'they were (being), they used to be', beside oedynt (ual y bydynt yn eisted 'as they were sitting')
un: un (un) — one; numeral/adjective (un dyrnaut 'one blow') · also 'same' (yn un ansawd 'in the same appearance'; yr un ford 'the same way') and the pronoun 'one (of them)' (Un a gyuodes 'one rose')
dim: dim — anything, nothing; indefinite pronoun (ny russya dim ragot 'nothing will obstruct before you')
wrthunt: wrth (wrth) + wynt — 'to, at, towards them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (a uu wrthunt 'there was to them'); no mutation
arglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m., term of address
mi: mi — 1 sg. independent/emphatic pronoun 'I' (mi a wnn 'I know')
af: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 sg. present/future 'I go, I will go' (a af 'will go')
geissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; verbal noun in -aw (ar geissaw eu llad 'on seeking to kill them'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'on'
chwedleu: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, talk; noun f., plural chwedleu (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); ch- does not mutate here
dioer: dioer — assuredly, indeed; an oath, a worn-down Duw a wyr 'God knows'
nyt: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not, it is not', spelling before a vowel or in emphasis (nyt teilygdawt)
da: da — good; adjective, also 'goods, wealth' as a noun (treulaw dy da 'spending your wealth')
dy: dy — 'your' (sg.); possessive pronoun, causes soft mutation (dy gerennyd 'your friendship') · also written for the affixed pronoun di 'you' after the presentative wely (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son')
gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel') · also soft after wrth (Reit oed im wrth gynghor 'I could do with counsel') and after pa (a pha gynghor 'and what counsel')
uynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun, soft-mutated after e/y (e uynet e gyscu 'to go to sleep')
honn: hon (hon) — 'this' (f.); variant spelling of hon (no'r ulwydyn honn 'than this year')
uyg: uy (fy) — my; possessive, here spelt uyg before k-: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation the noun would take (uyg kyuoeth = fy nghyfoeth 'my realm')
i: i — (1) emphatic independent pronoun 'I/me', echoing a verb or conjugated preposition (rof i, arnaf i); (2) spelling of y 'to' before a vowel or l/w (i waret); (3) spelling of y 'his' before some words (i wisc hela 'his hunting-dress') · (4) after ohonawch, probably the 2 pl. echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending (ohonawch i 'of you')
idi: idi (iddi) — to her; 3 sg. f. conjugated form of y 'to' (menegi... a wnaeth idi)
neb: neb (neb) — anyone; pronoun, used with a positive sense in relative/superlative clauses (o'r a welsei neb 'that anyone had seen') · also 'anyone' under a negative = 'no one' (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue') · also in y neb a 'the one who/to whom' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'the one from whom one ought to take it')
hut: hut (hud) — magic, illusion, enchantment; noun m. (ystyr hut 'a meaning of magic')
wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat) · also soft as the object of a verb, with an adverb between (ny welsynt eiryoet wlat gyuanhedach 'they had never seen a more settled land')
ef: ef (ef) — 'he, him'; independent 3 sg. m. pronoun
gan: gan (gan) — with, by; preposition, softening the next word; possession is 'with' a person or thing (oed gan y march 'the horse had', literally 'was with the horse'); y gan 'from' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'); base of gennyf, ganthaw, genthi etc. · also 'from', without y (ny chaffei namyn yr un atteb gan y gwraged 'she would get only the same answer from the women'; yny gigleu gan lawer 'until he heard from many')
uanawydan: Proper name — Manawydan; soft-mutated (m>u) as a person addressed, vocative (Kyuodwch, Uanawydan uab Llyr 'rise, Manawydan son of Llŷr') · also soft after at 'to' (at Uanawydan 'to Manawydan') and after e gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also soft after o marking the doer and after y 'to' (o Uanawydan; y Uanawydan), in apposition after ef (ef Uanawydan) and as the subject straight after the verb (y llunyei Uanawydan)
gyrchwys: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after y (y gyrchwys 'he made for')
doeth: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. preterite 'came' (a doeth 'and came')
dyn: dyn (dyn) — man, person; noun m. (y dyn eithaf 'the farthest man')
thy: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m.; spirant-mutated (t>th) after na 'neither' (na thy 'nor any house')
nac: nac — (1) negative used in a direct answer, repeating the verb, 'no' (Nac attygaf 'I will not'); (2) 'nor' before a vowel (nac ymdidan) · also negative imperative 'do not' (nac arch dim 'do not ask anything') · also Nac ef 'no', literally 'not it', refusing a proposal (Nac ef, heb y Manawydan 'No, said Manawydan')
welei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect 'he saw' (welei), soft-mutated after a (ef a welei lannerch) · also 'would see' (neu ynteu a welei rywedawt 'or else he would see a wonder')
ual: ual (fel) — as, like; conjunction/preposition (ual hynn 'like this') · also 'so that' (ual yd ymglywynt 'so that they could hear one another'; ual y bydynt gadarnach 'so that they would be stronger') and 'how' (sef ual yd eistedyssant 'that is how they sat')
am: am — preposition 'about, around; concerning' (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck'; am dir a dayar 'about land') · also 'for, in return for' (am y gam 'for his wrong'; am pob un 'for each one')
llawr: llawr (llawr) — ground, floor; noun m., base form (y'r llawr 'to the ground')
uaen: maen (maen) — stone; noun m. (ae o uaen guerthuawr 'or of a precious stone'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the preposition o 'of'
uch: uch (uwch) — above, over; preposition (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also 'high' as adjective/adverb, comparative in yn uch no bwrd y llong 'higher than the ship's board'
benn: penn (pen) — head, top, end; noun m.; soft-mutated (p>b) after ar 'on' (ar benn gossed 'on top of a mound'; ar benn y pethewnos 'at the end of the fortnight') · also soft after y 'his' (gauas y benn 'found his head') and after am 'about' (am benn hwnnw 'about that one's head') · also soft after a preceding adjective (Yspydawt Urdaul Benn 'the Hospitality of the Honoured Head') and after the feminine noun yspydawt (Yspydaut Benn 'the Hospitality of the Head')
arnunt: ar — conjugated preposition 'on them' (Sef lliw oed arnunt 'this was the colour that was on them')
dyuot: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; verbal noun (a dyuot y Lynn Cuch 'and coming to Glyn Cuch')
ymauael: ymauael (ymafael) — to seize hold, grasp; verbal noun (yn ymauael a'r ebawl 'seizing the foal'); no mutation
dwylaw: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., dual/plural dwylaw 'hands', from dwy llaw 'two hands' (a'y dwylaw 'and her hands'); no mutation
draet: troet (troed) — foot; plural traet (traed), soft-mutated (t > d) after y 'his' (am y draet 'on his feet')
seuyll: seuyll (sefyll) — to stand; verbal noun (yn seuyll yn y lle 'standing at once'); no mutation
dwyn: dwyn (dwyn) — to carry, bring; verbal noun (dwyn y dwy dyrnas yn un 'bringing the two kingdoms into one') · also 'to pass, spend, experience' a time (dwyn yspeit digriuach 'to pass a merrier time'); sense from context
lywenyd: llywenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (diruawr lywenyd 'huge gladness'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preceding adjective diruawr
gantaw: gan (gan) — 'with him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt gantaw (hyspys oed gantaw 'it was known to him'); no mutation
dywedut: dywedut (dweud) — to say, speak; verbal noun/infinitive
geir: geir (gair) — word; noun m.; geir is the Middle Welsh spelling, no mutation after un with a masculine noun (un geir 'one word') · also 'near, by', a spelling of ger (ymauael a'r ebawl geir y uwng 'seizing the foal by its mane')
diwed: diwed (diwedd) — end, close; noun m., d spells dd; radical after the article y (yn y diwed 'in the end')
dyd: dyd (dydd) — day; noun m. (y dyd 'the day'; dyd da 'good day')
diheu: diheu (diau) — certain, doubtless; adjective (ny bo diheu gantaw hynny 'who would not be sure of that'); no mutation
chaei: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might get' (ony chaei dial 'unless he got vengeance'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ony 'unless'
daw: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. present 'comes' (na daw uy nei attaf i 'does my nephew not come to me?'); after na; d also spells dd, so any softening does not show
mywn: y mywn (i mewn) — in, inside; adverbial phrase (yn dyuot y mywn 'coming in') · also prepositional 'in' (y mywn gogof 'in a cave')
riannon: Riannon (Rhiannon) — proper name, daughter of Heueyd Hen
arnaw: ar — conjugated preposition 'on him, on it' (llithiau dy erchwys dy hun arnaw 'feeding your own pack on it')
mae: bot (bod) — to be; irregular present 3 sg. 'is, there is' (y mae arnat o anryded) · also interrogative 'where is?' (Mae yr yniuer …? 'where is the company …?')
hi: hi — 'she, her'; independent 3 sg. f. pronoun
gedymdeith: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; noun m., soft-mutated as object (yn gedymdeith 'as a companion') · also soft after 'y 'his' (a'y gedymdeith 'and his companion')
di: di — 'you' (sg.), echoing pronoun after a verb or possessive (y pryny di; dy gerennyd di); also the object 'you' (ni ladaf i di)
th: 'th — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'th, i'th, dy'th etc.: 'your' (possessive) or 'you' (object)
kyfranc: kyfranc (cyfranc) — encounter, event, adventure, the story of an event; noun m.; radical after eu 'their' (Eu kyfranc wy 'their story')
oll: oll (oll) — all, wholly; adverb/adjective intensifying a preceding noun (yr arueu oll 'all the armour')
ys: ys (ys) — 'it is'; copula particle introducing a predicate, esp. in time expressions (ys blwydyn 'it is a year' = for a year) · also the infixed 3 sg. object 's 'it' after pei (pei ys guelwn 'if I saw it') · also 'below, under', is, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed' · also before the verb in ac aduyd ys kymeraf 'and perhaps I will take' (the Red Book atuyd ys kymeraf): perhaps the particle, perhaps the infixed 's 'it' after aduyd; uncertain
drwc: drwc (drwg) — evil, harm, wrong; noun m. (ny chewch un drwc 'you will get no harm'); no mutation
chan: can (can) — since, because; conjunction, spirant-mutated (k > ch) after a 'and' (A chan derw yt 'and since it has befallen you') · also the preposition can 'with, by' (= gan), spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chan hynn o wyrda 'and with these noblemen'; a chan pawb 'and by everyone')
hwnnw: hwnnw (hwnnw) — 'that' (m.); demonstrative (y dyd hwnnw 'that day') · also pronoun 'that one' (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man'; yw hwnnw 'that is it')
allan: allan — out, forth; adverb ('o hynny allan' 'from then on')
traws: traws (traws) — across, athwart, crosswise; noun/adjective in ar traws 'across' (ar traws yr auon 'across the river'); radical after ar
uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uot yn colli 'that he was losing', lit. 'his being losing')
gwr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m. (y gwr a oed yn lle Arawn 'the man who was in Arawn's place')
hitheu: hitheu (hithau) — conjunctive form of hi 'she', 'she for her part'
porth: porth (porth) — gate, gateway, entrance; noun m. (y porth 'the gate'); no mutation
welas: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. preterite 'saw', soft-mutated after relative y (yny welas y llys a'r kyuanned)
agoret: agoret (agored) — open; adjective, past participle in -et (yn agoret 'open'); no mutation (vowel)
bu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (a uu 'was'; Llawen uu 'glad was')
arganuot: arganuot (arganfod) — to perceive, discover; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaeth (arganuot y bolyeu crwyn a wnaeth 'perceiving the skin-bags he did')
attaw: at — conjugated preposition 'to him' (y marchawc a doeth attaw 'the horseman came to him')
och: och (och) — alas; interjection of dismay (Och! heb y Riannon 'Alas, said Rhiannon')
uy: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, triggers nasal mutation (uy anryded; uy nghyffes; uy gherennyd)
wney: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. present/future in -i (wnei) 'you do, you will do' (A wney ditheu gynghor arall? 'will you do another counsel?'; Iawn a wney 'you do right'); g lost by soft mutation after the particle a (interrogative, relative)
nos: nos (nos) — night; noun f. (y nos honno 'that night')
nywl: nywl (niwl) — mist, fog; noun m. (gawat o nywl 'a shower of mist'; yn ol y nywl 'after the mist'); n does not change after o or the article
wynteu: wynt (hwynt) — they, for their part; conjunctive 3 pl. pronoun (Wynteu hagen ni wybuyssynt)
pann: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction, spelt pann (Pann doethont 'when they came'); causes soft mutation, not shown on d- (dd)
kicua: Kicua (Cigfa) — proper name, the wife Pryderi chose, daughter of Gwyn Gohoyw; no mutation
uerch: merch (merch) — daughter, girl; noun f., softened after a woman's name (Riannon uerch Heueyd 'Rhiannon daughter of Hefeydd') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uerch y urenhin 'as daughter to the king')
gwyn: Proper name — Gwyn (gwyn also 'white, fair'), father of Heilyn, in Heilyn uab Gwyn Hen 'Heilyn son of Gwyn the Old'; radical after uab
gwreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., meaning as context decides (a'y wreic 'and his wife')
nat: na, nat (nad) — 'that … not'; negative conjunction of a subordinate clause, nat before a vowel (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there')
namyn: namyn (namyn) — except, but; conjunction (namyn ti 'but you')
well: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good', soft-mutated as the object of kyuarch (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you') · also soft as a comparative standing after its noun (seith cantref well 'seven better cantrefs'; heldir well 'a better hunting-land')
genti: gan (gan) — 'with her'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. f., spelt genti (a chanawon genti 'and whelps with her'); no mutation
byw: byw — alive; adjective (ny byd byw ef 'he will not be alive')
cam: cam (cam) — wrong, injustice; noun m. (cam a wnaeth 'he did wrong'); no mutation (fronted object)
wyt: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. present 'you are' (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
os: os (os) — if; conjunction of a real condition (os hynny a uynny 'if that is what you want')
rac: rac (rhag) — before, lest, to prevent, for fear of; preposition (dyro ui idaw rac anglot yt 'give me to him to spare you dishonour') · also 'from' after verbs of saving (waret rac hynn 'to deliver from this')
ouyn: ofyn (ofn) — fear; noun m., u for the v-sound (nyt oes arnaf i ouyn 'I have no fear', literally 'there is no fear on me') · also 3 sg. present of gouyn (gofyn) 'asks', with g lost by soft mutation after a (ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'); a different word from ofyn 'fear' · also 2 sg. imperative of gouyn (gofyn) 'ask', g lost by soft mutation after na (na ouyn di yni y mab 'do not ask us for the boy') · also verbal noun gouyn 'asking', g- lost by soft mutation after heb 'without' (heb ouyn 'without asking') and after y 'to' (y ouyn idaw 'to ask of him')
rodaf: rodi (rhoi) — to give, put; 1 sg. present/future 'I will give/put' (mi a'th rodaf di)
it: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelling variant with single t (achos it heuyt)
weleisti: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 sg. preterite weleist with the pronoun ti written on, 'you saw', soft-mutated after a (noc a weleisti 'than what you saw')
noc: no (na) — than; spelling before a vowel (noc a uu 'than what was')
keffy: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 2 sg. present/future 'you will get' (y keffy uy gherennyd)
ui: ui (fi) — me; object pronoun after an imperative (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here') · also the softened pronoun 'I' after a verb (Ny allaf ui arnaf a dywedy di uyth 'I cannot bring myself to do what you say') and as the second, emphatic pronoun in mi ui 'I myself' (A mi ui a rodaf 'and I myself will give'); soft-mutated from mi · also after gwae 'woe' (guae ui 'woe is me')
tra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (tra deweis wrthyt ti 'while I kept silent') · also (2) 'very', before an adjective with spirant mutation (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty'); (3) 'while' with the verb sometimes soft-mutated (tra barhaud)
uelly: uelly (felly) — thus, so, in that way; adverb, u for the v-sound (no mutation: f is its own first letter); often written y uelly with a particle y (attep y uelly 'an answer thus'; ac y uelly guare 'and so playing')
rof: rwng (rhwng) + i — conjugated preposition 'between me' (y rof i a Duw 'between me and God')
bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk) · also the conjunction 'if' (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them')
ieuengtit: ieuengtit (ieuenctid) — youth, early part; noun f. (yn ieuengtit y dyd 'in the youth of the day' = early morning)
gadwn: gadu (gadael) — to let, allow; 1 pl. present 'we allow, will allow' (-wn) (nys gadwn 'we will not allow it'); no mutation (g- radical after ny + 's)
rot: y rwng (rhwng) — between; y rot is the 2 sg. conjugated form 'between you', modern rhyngot (y rot a'th uarchogyon 'between you and your horsemen'), as y rof 'between me' in y rof i a Duw
titheu: ti (ti) — you, for your part; conjunctive 2 sg. pronoun
uit: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperative 'let it be' (bit); soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after the negative na (na uit kyn drymhet 'let it not be so heavy')
arnat: ar — conjugated preposition 'on you' (sg.) (y mae arnat o anryded 'there is rank on you'; a'm ansawd arnat ti)
gedymdeithas: kedymdeithas (cydymdeithas) — fellowship, companionship; noun f., soft-mutated after y (kedymdeithas y ryngthunt 'fellowship between them')
genhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me' (eres genhyf 'strange with me'; ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); the gan 'with' of opinion; no mutation
herwyd: herwyd (herwydd) — in respect of, according to; preposition (yn herwyd ymlad 'in respect of fighting')
yna: yna (yna) — then; adverb (Yna y rodes Arawn y furuf)
kymry: Kymry (Cymru) — Wales (strictly the Welsh, Cymry, here the country); proper name; the nasal mutation of yg Kymry 'in Wales' (yng Nghymru) is shown only on the preceding yg
llywenyd: llywenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (digrifwch a llywenyd)
uorwyn: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden; noun f., soft-mutated in address (A uorwyn 'O maiden'), after the article (y uorwyn 'the maiden') and after o (o uorwyn 'of maiden') · also soft after am 'about' (am uorwyn kystal 'about a maiden so good')
achaws: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m. ('Pa achaws' 'what reason, why')
ie: ie — yes; particle of assent, taking up what was just said
eneit: eneit (enaid) — soul; used in address as an endearment 'dear one, my soul' (a dos y eisted, eneit 'and go to sit, friend')
yni: y (i) + ni — 'to us'; conjugated preposition, 1 pl., variant of ynni (na ouyn di yni y mab 'do not ask us for the boy'); no mutation
kyrchwn: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, go to; 1 pl. imperative 'let us make for' in -wn (Kyrchwn Loygyr 'let us make for England'); radical
yw: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. copula 'is', used in equative sentences (Sef yw hwnnw, Hafgan)
in: y (i) + ni — 'to us, for us'; conjugated preposition 1 pl., spelt in (ys guell in 'it is better for us'); no mutation
llawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, base form (yn llawen)
ni: ni — (1) 1 pl. pronoun 'we/us' (yd ymdidanyssam ni); (2) negative particle, spelling variant of ny before some verbs (ni ladaf, ni bu)
wnawn: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 pl. present/future 'we shall make' (ni a wnawn yr oet 'we shall make the appointment'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the particle a
lloygyr: Proper name — Lloegr, England (Lloygyr beside Lloegyr); radical (Kyrchu Lloygyr 'making for England'; yn Lloygyr 'in England')
greft: crefft (crefft) — craft, trade, skill; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) as the direct object directly after the verb (cheisswn greft 'let us seek a craft'); cause the soft mutation of an object after an inflected verb
gwneuthum: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. preterite 'I did' (a wneuthum i yrot ti 'what I did for you')
gynt: kynt (cynt) — (1) 'swifter', comparative of buan 'swift', softened after a noun (warch gynt 'a swifter horse'); (2) 'before, formerly', the softened adverb, modern gynt (no'r dyd gynt 'than the day before')
wr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ansyberwyt uwy ar wr) · also soft after y 'to' (y wr 'to a man, to a husband') · also soft in address (A wr 'O man') and after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw wr 'what kind of man') · also subject directly after a negated verb, soft-mutated (Ny doey wr mawr 'no great man would come')
kyuurd: kyuurd (cyfurdd) — of equal rank, of the same degree; adjective, kyf- 'co-' + urdd 'rank' (morwyn gystal, kyuurd 'a maiden so good, of equal rank'); no mutation
geluydyt: celfyddyd (celfyddyd) — craft, trade, art, skill; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after pa 'what' (Pa geluydyt 'what craft')
cordwal: cordwal (cordwal) — cordovan leather, fine leather, from Cordoba; noun m.; radical after the article y
teccaf: tec (teg) — fair, pretty; superlative 'fairest' (yr ardurn teccaf a welsei neb)
gauas: caffael (cael) — to get, find, reach; 3 sg. preterite 'got', soft-mutated after a (a gauas 'got, reached')
dref: tref (tref) — town, homestead, settlement; noun f., soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (ar y dref 'on the town') · also soft after holl (yn yr holl dref 'in the whole town') and after y 'to' (y dref arall 'to another town')
dechreussant: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 pl. preterite in -ssant 'they began' (A'r gyuedach a dechreussant 'and the carousing they began'); no mutation shown after the relative a (the soft mutation of d- is not written)
arall: arall — other, another; adjective (yr erchwys arall 'the other pack') · also pronoun 'another (woman)' (heb arall 'said another')
eskidyeu: esgid (esgid) — shoe; noun f., plural eskidyeu (modern esgidiau) (y'r eskidyeu 'for the shoes'); radical after the article
eureit: eureit (euraid) — golden; adjective, from aur 'gold' (gwisc eureit 'a golden garment')
holl: holl (holl) — all, whole; adjective, precedes its noun causing soft mutation (yr holl gyuoeth 'the whole realm')
grydyon: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker; noun m., plural in -yon (modern cryddion); soft-mutated (c>g) after gan 'with, among' (gan grydyon)
eidaw: eiddo (eiddo) — that which belongs to someone, 'his'; the independent possessive in 3 sg. m. (yr eidaw ef 'his'; pa darpar oed yr eidaw 'what purpose was his'); no mutation (vowel)
hun: hun (hun) — self, own; also 'sleep' as a separate noun by context (e hunan/e hun 'himself'; kymryt hun 'to take sleep')
geffit: caffael (cael) — to get, have; impersonal imperfect (subjunctive/habitual) 'was got, could be had' in -it (tra geffit gan Uanawydan 'while there was to be got from Manawydan'); soft-mutated (c>g) after tra 'while'
eskit: esgid (esgid) — shoe; noun f. (nac eskit na hossan 'neither shoe nor hose'); radical after nac
hossan: hosan (hosan) — stocking, hose; noun f., ss for s (na hossan 'nor hose'); radical after na, h- not mutated
phrynit: prynu (prynu) — to buy; impersonal imperfect 'was bought' in -it (ny phrynit gan gyfrwyd 'it was not bought from a saddler'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny and after hyt na
ereill: arall (arall) — other; plural ereill, the plural form of the adjective (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); modern eraill
dreulwys: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after a (a dreulwys trwy digrifwch 'he spent in amusement')
crydyon: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker; noun m., plural in -yon (modern cryddion) (y crydyon 'the shoemakers'); radical after the article
dala: dala (dal) — to hold, seize, take on; verbal noun (dechreuis gwyr y wlat dala trymuryt 'the men of the land began to take sorrow'); no mutation
wrthaw: wrth (wrth) + ef — conjugated preposition 'to/at him' (a dywedut ual hynn wrthaw) · also in y wrthaw, e wrthaw 'from him, away from him'
menegi: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, relate; verbal noun (menegi y holl gyfranc a wnaeth idi)
wedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, spelt without g, as in modern wedi (wedy bwyta 'after the eating'); the loss of g is a variant spelling, there is no clear softening word
duunaw: duunaw (dyuno) — to agree, come to one mind; verbal noun in -aw, du- + un 'one' (duunaw ar y lad ef 'agreeing on killing him'); radical
lad: lladd (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun (am lad o honaf uu hun uy mab 'for my killing of my own son'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition am · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive 'e 'his' (na'e lad 'nor his killing')
pam: pam (pam) — why; interrogative adverb (Pam y kymerwn inheu hynny? 'why should we take that?'), followed by the particle y
hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs')
tayogeu: taeog (taeog) — villein, serf, churl; noun m., plural in -eu (tayogeu, modern taeogion) (llad y tayogeu racco 'killing those churls yonder'); radical after the article y
eissoes: eissoes (eisoes) — yet, nevertheless; adverb (Ac eissoes ni eill ef 'and yet he cannot'); no mutation (vowel)
gychwynnwys: kychwynnu (cychwyn) — to set out; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after a (ef a gychwynnwys 'he set out')
chyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a chyrchu y bordeu 'and making for the tables')
chyuanhedu: kyfanhedu (cyfanheddu) — to inhabit, settle, populate; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a'y 'and it' (a'y chyuanhedu 'and to settle it')
nit: nyt (nid) — negative particle 'not, there is not', spelling before a vowel (Nit oes; Nit yttoydwn)
digriuach: digrif (digrifach) — more pleasant, merrier; comparative of digrif 'pleasant, merry', spelt digriuach; adjective after its noun (yspeit digriuach 'a merrier time'); no mutation
buassei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had been' (megys y buassei y mab 'how the boy had been'), -ssei; no mutation after the particle y
eil: eil (ail) — second; ordinal numeral (yr eil 'the second')
trydyd: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal (ar y trydyd 'at the third')
nachaf: nachaf (no modern form) — behold, lo; presentative particle that sets the scene before the eyes (nachaf un o'r llongeu 'behold one of the ships'); no mutation
kyuot: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 2 sg. imperative 'rise!' (kyuot y uynyd ar uyrr 'rise up quickly')
oreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good', softened after a feminine noun (y neges oreu 'the best errand') · also soft as predicate after bu (yn gystal ac y bu oreu 'as good as he was best')
byt: byt (byd) — world; noun m. (o helgwn y byt 'of the hunting dogs of the world')
dwf: twf (twf) — growth, stature; noun m. (a uei uawr y dwf a'e ueint 'that was big in his growth and his size'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the possessive y 'his'
welsei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had seen', soft-mutated after o'r a (o'r a welsei ef)
treulaw: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); verbal noun, base form
uynhaf: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 1 sg. present 'I want' (na uynhaf 'I do not want'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the negative na
auory: auory (yfory) — tomorrow; adverb (o'r dyd auory 'from the day tomorrow')
bore: bore (bore) — morning; noun m.; radical after the article y (y bore 'the morning'; the scribe leaves a blank before it)
uynnu: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; verbal noun, soft-mutated (m>u) after dy 'your' (wrth dy uynnu 'according to your wish')
daruot: daruot (darfod) — to finish, be finished, happen; verbal noun, with y/i of the person (kynn daruot idaw ymgueiraw 'before he had finished making ready')
pob: pob (pob) — each, every; adjective (pob un 'each one')
doi: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. imperfect 'used to come, came' (kystal y doi y gof 'as well came to mind')
thrannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; noun/adverb, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A thrannoeth) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no thrannoeth 'than the next day')
uedwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uedwl) · also soft-mutated (m>u) after pa 'what' (pa uedwl yw yr eidunt 'what intention is theirs')
pwy: pwy (pwy) — who; interrogative pronoun (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
uyn: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. present 'wants' (A uyn ef dyuot y'r tir 'does he want to come ashore?'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the interrogative particle a
gwnn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. present 'I know', g often dropped after ny (ny wnn i 'I do not know')
dechreuis: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 sg. preterite 'began' (y dechreuis gwyr y wlat dala trymuryt 'the men of the land began to take sorrow'); no mutation after the particle y
tryded: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal, feminine form tryded (trydedd) (A honno oed tryded prif rieni 'and she was the third chief ...'); no mutation (soft mutation after predicative yn is not written: yn tryded)
degach: tec (teg) — fair, pleasant; comparative degach 'pleasanter' (yn degach genthi 'pleasanter to her'); soft-mutated (t>d) after predicative yn
meuyl: meuyl (mefl) — shame, disgrace; noun m., used in the oath meuyl im 'shame on me' · also meuyl ar 'shame on' (Meuyl ar uy maryf i 'shame on my beard')
ony: ony (oni) — unless, until; conjunction ('no, unless …'), causes spirant mutation of c, p, t (ony chyuyt 'unless there rise') · also with soft mutation of g (ony wybydaf i 'if I do not find out')
duc: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry, take; 3 sg. preterite 'took' (Ruthyr a duc 'he made a rush', literally 'a rush he took'); no mutation shown after a (d for dd)
yt: y 'to' — conjugated preposition, 2 sg. 'to you', modern iti, spelt yt beside itt and itti (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good'; rac anglot yt 'for fear of dishonour to you'; ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'; derw yt 'it has befallen you')
wybydaf: gwybot (gwybod) — to know, find out; 1 sg. present with future sense 'I find out' (ony wybydaf i pa dileith yssyd 'if I do not find out what destruction it is'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after ony
chymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, put on; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymryt lloppaneu 'and putting on clouts')
arueu: arueu (arfau) — arms, armour; noun pl. (yny dyrr yr arueu oll 'so that all the armour breaks')
gwylat: gwylat (gwylio) — to watch, keep watch; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethont (Gwylat a wnaethont wynteu dalym o'r nos 'they kept watch a while of the night'); no mutation
uryt: bryt (bryd) — mind, intent; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uryt 'into his mind') · also ar uryt 'in the mind of', to the eye of, soft after ar (ar uryt y neb a'y guelei 'to the eye of anyone who saw it')
wylat: gwylat (gwylio) — to watch, keep watch; verbal noun (y wylat y mab 'to watch the boy'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to'
aeth: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. preterite 'went' (a'y vreic a aeth attaw 'and his wife went to him')
byd: bot (bod) — to be; used two ways: 3 sg. future 'will be' (uyd elsewhere) and, with y-, the vivid present ual y byd 'as he is' · also 2 sg. imperative 'be!' (byd ditheu a'r got honn genhyt 'you be there with this bag')
hanner: hanner (hanner) — half; noun m. (yn deu hanner 'into two halves')
twryf: twrf (twrf) — noise, din, tumult; noun m., spelt twryf in the epithet Twryf Uliant 'tumult of flood' (Teirnon Twryf Uliant); no mutation
mwyhaf: mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'most', spelt mwyhaf (y gwr mwyhaf a gery 'the man you love most')
ellit: gallu (gallu) — to be able; impersonal imperfect 'could be' (a ellit a'r meirych 'that could be had from the horses'); g- lost by soft mutation after the relative a
wydat: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. imperfect 'he knew' (na wydat pwy a'e lladei 'that he did not know who was killing them'; the Red Book wydyat); g- lost by soft mutation after na
uyd: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present/future 'is, will be' (byd), soft-mutated after a or a predicate (Dilesteir uyd dy hynt; yny uyd Hafgan)
guan: gwanu (gwanu) — to stab, thrust; verbal noun (guan y dan y meirych 'thrusting under the horses'); gu- for gw-; no mutation
phob: pob (pob) — every, each; adjective (a phob nos Calanmei 'and every May-eve'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
hynt: hynt — way, course, journey; noun f. (dy hynt 'your way')
racdunt: rac (rhag) + wynt — conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'before them' (modern rhagddynt), in -dunt; idiomatic 'on, ahead of them' (a gerdassant racdunt 'walked on their way'), and 'on their account, before them' elsewhere (a lwydwys racdunt 'prospered before them'; dygywys … racdunt 'was galling because of them')
gantunt: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'with them' (a'r gennadwri honno gantunt 'with that message with them')
rwng: rwng (rhwng) — between; preposition, base uninflected form
taraw: taraw (taro) — to strike, hit; verbal noun, fronted before a wnai (taraw a wnai pob un dyrnawt 'each one would strike a blow')
ym: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelling variant before p/m/b (hyt ym Penn Llwyn Diarwya; ym perued) · also bot 1 pl. present 'we are' (yd ym y gyt 'we are together'; llibin yd ym pob blwydyn 'wretched that we are every year') · also 'my', a by-form of uy, in the oath ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God' (the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); the nasal mutation it brings is not written
plith: plith (plith) — midst; noun m., in ym plith 'among' (ym plith hynn o niuer 'among this (much) of company')
mwy: mwy (mwy) — more, greater; comparative of mawr (mwy yw gan Uendigeituran no chenyt ti 'it is greater to Bendigeidfran than to you'); no mutation (fronted predicate); also mwy dwyweith 'twice as big'
neu: neu (neu) — (1) 'or' (kymriw neu archolleu 'injury or wounds'; neu ynteu 'or else'); (2) the affirmative particle neu 'lo, indeed' before a verb, neut before a vowel, neur with infixed 'r (see neut, neir)
adar: aderyn (aderyn) — bird; plural adar 'birds'; in the title Adar Riannon 'the Birds of Rhiannon', the plural noun followed by a name in the genitive; radical
ohonunt: o (o) + wynt — 'of them, from them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (kyscu a wnaeth pawb ohonunt 'every one of them slept'); no mutation
wy: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelling variant (heb wy 'said they') · also emphatic 'them' after a conjugated preposition (ganthunt wy 'from them', ohonunt wy 'of them')
eithyr: eithyr (eithr) — except; conjunction/preposition (eithyr gadu 'except to leave')
pedestric: pedestric — meaning disputed: 'going on foot' (o pedestric 'on foot') or 'speed, running' (it is also said of a horse); noun, a borrowing from Latin pedester 'on foot'
kerdwys: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go, travel; 3 sg. preterite 'walked' (y kerdwys ef 'he went about'); radical after particle y
dodi: dodi (dodi) — to put; verbal noun (dodi y deudroet yn y got 'to put his two feet in the bag'; dodi llef ar y gorn 'to give a blast on the horn')
chadw: cadw (cadw) — to keep; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a chadw kywirdeb 'and keeping faithfulness')
